title: Winged zebrafish - 3D-printable anatomical kit
hypothetical_note: HYPOTHETICAL: this piece belongs to the design 'winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish', not to any described animal. It was generated from a parameter set, not observed.
what_this_is_not: The geometry is SCHEMATIC. Organ shapes, sizes and positions are generated from a parameter set, not measured from a specimen.
The one evidence-backed proportion is the pectoral fin: pectoral_len_over_SL and the span and area that follow from it. Everything else is a plausible arrangement.
Cell tokens are MARKERS for recorded cell types, not models of cells. No cell-level geometry exists in the source and none was invented.
The animal is a DESIGN, not a described species. No fish like this has been observed.
Any glide figure attached to this geometry is UNVERIFIED. See the README.

source_mesh.units_and_axes: glTF Y-up; head at +X, back at +Y, the fish's left side at -Z. The adult / resolved set has SL = 0.82 model units; earlier growth stages are built at their TRUE relative size SL(age)/SL(adult), so development plays as real growth. standard_length_m = 0.0388 m sets the metres per model unit.
source_mesh.basis_note: SL = 0.82 model units ties to standard_length_m = 0.0388 m. Standard length in fish morphometrics runs to the hypural plate, not to the posterior tip of the skin; measuring the skin tip gives 0.8528 units and every derived number comes out 4% small.

fit_test_coupon.how_to_use: Print flat on the build platform. Try a peg in each socket. The tightest socket a peg enters by hand without forcing, and holds without glue, is the clearance to build the kit at. Report that number back and the kit is rebuilt to it.

ballast_bore.sized_for: a 2.5 mm steel rod 9 mm long, about 0.35 g, which is what the first-order stability estimate says is needed for a +10% margin

stability_basis.METHOD: FIRST-ORDER, FLAT-PLATE, PECTORAL FINS ONLY: the neutral point is the quarter-chord of the pectoral planform's mean aerodynamic chord, ignoring the body, the median fins, the caudal fin, downwash, sweep and dihedral. It says the question is live; it does not say what the answer is.

ff_fins_solid_1to1_GLIDER.UNVERIFIED: C_Lmax 0.78 is Park & Choi's measurement on a ~20 cm STUFFED REAL flying fish. At 4 cm the Reynolds number is roughly 5x lower and the flow regime differs, so the coefficient does not transfer. No tunnel test, no flight test, no stability analysis beyond the first-order estimate above.

stability_first_order.verdict: CG is AFT of the estimated neutral point: statically UNSTABLE in pitch by this first-order estimate; nose ballast would be needed
stability_first_order.CAVEAT: This is a flat-plate, first-order estimate. The neutral point is taken as the quarter-chord of the pectoral planform's mean aerodynamic chord and ignores the body, the median fins, the caudal fin, downwash, and any sweep or dihedral. It is an order-of-magnitude check on whether the question 'does it need ballast' even arises. It is NOT a stability analysis and nothing here has been tested in a tunnel or in flight.

They are merged into chunky blocks rather than inflated 10-80x, and every merge is recorded per part. The 120 mm kit keeps them separate.

kit_120mm_note.status: structural parts built and verified in scratch; not published, because the 1:1 kit is the delivered kit. Cell tokens and register cards were designed for this scale, where they are handleable.

failed the watertight / normals check

verification.method: Blender 4.2.23 bmesh, per STL: (1) every edge has exactly two faces -> watertight; (2) every edge is contiguous, i.e. its two faces wind in opposite directions -> no inverted normals anywhere, and unlike comparing a face normal against the direction of the centre of mass this is correct for concave shapes; (3) no loose vertices or edges; (4) signed volume > 0, so the consistent orientation points outward. Minimum wall is MEASURED by casting a ray inward from each sampled vertex and taking the shortest hit, not assumed.
verification.min_feature_rule: no part's longest dimension may be under the stated handleable minimum; parts under it are merged into their parent and the merge is recorded
